subject: Martin Luther King Jr. Day Celebration
overview: The West Medford Community Center hosted its Martin Luther King Jr. Day celebration, featuring musical performances, poetry, community awards, and a keynote address on racial equity. Participants also observed the 90th anniversary of the community center and engaged in an interactive community-building exercise.

items.title: Welcome and Housekeeping
items.summary: Terry Carter opened the event with housekeeping announcements and invited attendees to introduce themselves to neighboring tables.

items.title: Invocation
items.summary: Pastor Tanner Turley offered the opening invocation, reflecting on Dr. King's determination and praying for racial justice and community growth.

items.title: Mayor's Welcoming Remarks
items.summary: Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn welcomed attendees, thanked community partners, and reflected on the event theme, 'Your Piece of the Dream.'

items.title: Musical Performance: 'Precious Lord, Take My Hand'
items.summary: Stacey Clayton and pianist Jonathan Fagan performed the traditional hymn 'Precious Lord, Take My Hand.'

items.title: Readings of Historic Prison Letters
items.summary: Vijaya Sundaram, Frances Nwajei, and Terry Carter read historical letters written from prison by Mahatma Gandhi, Nelson Mandela, and Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.

items.title: Spoken Word Performance: 'Alienation'
items.summary: Terry Carter and Jonathan Fagan performed 'Alienation,' a spoken word and jazz piece addressing the plight and treatment of immigrants.

items.title: Presentation of Drum Major Awards
items.summary: The center awarded Drum Major Awards to Reginald Graham, Earl and Tanya Howard, the late Rev. Dr. Florence Nottage King, and Johnny Reed.

items.title: Liturgical Dance Ministry
items.summary: Pastor Teresa Carter and fellow dancers ministered through a liturgical dance set to the song 'Believe For It.'

items.title: Interactive Community Puzzle Exercise
items.summary: Attendees assembled table puzzles bearing the phrase 'We all own a piece of the dream in creating beloved community' to demonstrate collective responsibility.

items.title: Poetry Readings
items.summary: Sharra Owens-Schwartz read Terry Carter's poem 'How Much Longer?' and Callie Owens-Schwartz read Langston Hughes's 'I Dream a World.'

items.title: Keynote Address
items.summary: Massachusetts Women of Color Coalition President and CEO Celia Johnston Blue delivered the keynote address on ongoing civil rights challenges, policy advocacy, and transformative solidarity.

items.title: Musical Performance: 'We Shall Overcome'
items.summary: Stacey Clayton, Jonathan Fagan, and the liturgical dance team led attendees in singing 'We Shall Overcome.'

items.title: Call to Action and Charge
items.summary: Nicole Mosalam presented a charge calling on participants to communicate honestly across differences, build interfaith bridges, and advocate for civic justice.

items.title: Closing Remarks and Acknowledgements
items.summary: Executive Director Lisa Crossman and Terry Carter noted the center's 90th anniversary and thanked the host parish, event sponsors, volunteers, and board members.
